transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I don’t know… my mom kind of made me come. I just can’t seem to do anything anymore. I mostly sit in my room, like, in the same clothes, and I know that sounds gross, but it’s like I can’t get myself to change or start anything.

I used to knit sometimes, and I had this journal with stickers on it—my cousin gave me the stickers, they were these little moons and cats—and I used to write in it or go for walks. Now I just… don’t. And when my mom asks what’s wrong, I barely even answer because it feels like too much energy to explain.
Have you been feeling sad or down most days?

I don’t know if it’s sad exactly. Like, people say “sad” and I think of crying at movies or when my grandma’s old dog died, because he had this little red collar and everyone kept saying he was “just a dog,” but he wasn’t really just a dog, you know?

I’m not… I don’t know. I feel kind of blank more than sad, maybe. Or tired. It’s hard to tell.
Before this started, have you ever had another period in your life when you felt this same kind of shut-down and unable to do things?

I don’t think so… not like this. I mean, I’ve had days where I didn’t want to do homework or I’d stay in bed too long, like after school breaks when everything felt weird, but this is different.

Now it’s more like I just can’t make myself start anything. I sit in my room, same clothes, and I’ll see my knitting stuff there—there’s this purple yarn I was using, it’s kind of scratchy actually—and I just don’t pick it up. Or my journal. I used to put little stickers in it and write random stuff, and now it just sits there.

And my mom asks me what’s wrong, and I know I should answer, but even talking feels like… too much. So, no, I don’t remember another time it was this shut-down.
Do you hear voices that other people can’t hear?

Um… I’m not really sure. Like, sometimes I think I hear something and then it’s just the heater or my mom in the kitchen, and our house makes weird noises at night anyway. The fridge does this clicking thing and it sounds almost like… not a voice, but like it’s trying to start talking, if that makes sense.

But voices that other people can’t hear… I don’t know. I haven’t really noticed it like that.
Has this shut-down feeling been there nearly every day for at least two weeks?

Yeah… I think so. It’s been most days, I guess. I kind of lose track because the days feel the same, like I’m just in my room and I’m still wearing the same clothes, and then my mom will say something about laundry and I’m like, oh, right, it’s been that long.

I don’t really do the things I used to. Like the knitting bag is just there, and my journal too, and I used to go walking sometimes but now I just… don’t. I can’t make myself start. Even answering my mom when she asks what’s wrong feels like a lot, like there’s no battery left. So… yeah, nearly every day.
Have you had a strong belief that other people would say is not true or doesn’t make sense?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t know if it “doesn’t make sense,” but my mom says I’m reading too much into it.

Since I was taking those college classes, I started noticing the school portal and the clinic practicum people would use these little wording changes in emails, or in comments on assignments, like… not obvious, but they’d switch how they said things. And it felt like they were marking me, like putting me in this category of someone they don’t want in healthcare.

Like if a comment says “consider” instead of “good start,” or the email has my name a certain way—sorry, that sounds stupid when I say it out loud, but it didn’t feel stupid. It felt like there was a pattern. My mom says they’re just regular messages and everyone gets comments like that, but I don’t think she’s looking at it closely enough.
Before this started, was there ever another time in your life when you felt like this for two weeks or longer?

I don’t know… before this, I mean, I had times where I was lazy or stayed in my room, but this feels different. Like now I mostly just can’t make myself do anything. I’ll sit there in the same clothes, and my knitting bag is right there, my journal too, and I keep thinking I should do it, or I should go for a walk, but then I just… don’t.

My mom asks what’s wrong and I barely even answer because it feels like too much effort, which sounds dramatic, but it’s like my brain won’t start. I don’t think it was like this before for this long. Not really.
Do you believe for sure that the emails and comments were meant to mark you and single you out?

Yeah… I mean, yes. I know my mom says that’s not what it is, that they’re just normal emails and comments, but it really felt—no, it more than felt like it. Since I was in those classes, the school portal and the clinic practicum people were changing little words, like in ways you’d miss if you weren’t paying attention.

And it wasn’t just one thing. It was the wording, the way they’d put comments on assignments, like they were marking me as someone they didn’t want in healthcare. Like they’d already decided something about me. My mom keeps saying, “They send those to everyone,” but she doesn’t see the pattern because she’s not the one it’s happening to.
Did you believe the school emails were marking and singling you out before this shut-down period started?

Yeah, it was before I kind of… shut down like this. It started when I was in those college classes, with the portal and the clinic practicum stuff. I’d read the emails and the assignment comments, and the wording would be just a little different, like they were marking me out as someone they didn’t want in healthcare.

And my mom kept saying they were just regular messages, like everyone gets them, but she wasn’t really looking at the details. I was. It was there before I stopped doing things so much.
Have you ever had a time lasting two weeks or more when you felt sad or depressed most of the day nearly every day?

I don’t know… I mean, sad like crying all day? Not really how I think of it. I get stuck, and then I end up in my room, and the days kind of pile up, but I don’t always label it “depressed.”

Sometimes my mom will ask if I’m sad, and I can’t explain it, because if I say yes then she starts asking all these other questions, and then I’m thinking about whether I sounded weird when I answered. So… I’m not sure. I can’t really say there was a clear two weeks where it was just sadness most of the day every day.
For two weeks or longer, have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah… I guess so. I used to knit sometimes, and I had this journal with like different pens—my mom bought me these ones that don’t smear, because I hate when it smears on the side of my hand—and I used to go walking too.

But now mostly I just sit in my room. Same clothes on, not really doing anything. It’s not like I decide, “I don’t like those things anymore,” it’s more like I can’t make myself start. My mom asks what’s wrong and I barely even have the energy to answer her, and then she thinks I’m ignoring her, but I’m not… I just can’t.
Have you ever had a time when you felt so energetic or unusually up that you needed much less sleep than usual?

I don’t think so… not like energetic. I mean, sometimes I don’t sleep right, but it’s not because I’m up doing a bunch of things or feeling great. It’s more like I’m just there, awake, and then the room feels too quiet, and I start noticing the little light from the charger, and then I remember I was supposed to wash that hoodie, but then I don’t.

So… no, I don’t really have those times where I’m unusually up and needing less sleep.
For at least one month, have you believed that the school emails and assignment comments were meant to mark and single you out?

Yeah… I mean, it was longer than a month. Since I was in those college classes, I kept noticing the school portal messages and the comments on assignments, like little wording changes… not obvious if you’re not looking, but they were there.

And then the clinic practicum people too, like the way they phrased things, it felt like they were marking me out, like saying I wasn’t someone they wanted in healthcare. My mom kept saying they were just normal emails, like “everyone gets those,” but she doesn’t see the pattern because she doesn’t read them the way I do.

It’s hard to explain because if I give one example it sounds small, but it kept happening.
Was there ever a time when you were having those beliefs about the emails, but you were not also feeling shut down or unable to do things?

Yeah… I think so. It wasn’t only when I was shut down. The email thing was already happening when I was still in the college classes, like before I was just sitting in my room all day.

I’d be looking at the school portal and the assignment comments, and the little wording changes were there. And the clinic practicum people too, the way they wrote things… it felt like they were marking me, like they knew I wasn’t supposed to be in healthcare. My mom kept saying, “That’s just a normal message,” but she doesn’t—she doesn’t look at it the same way.

Sorry, I’m trying to answer. Yes, the messages were still like that even when I wasn’t completely unable to do things.
Before this shut-down period began, did other people say you had become less emotional or less expressive than usual?

Before? Um… I don’t know if they said it exactly like that. My mom says I don’t answer her like I used to, but that’s more now, I think.

Mostly I just can’t make myself do anything anymore. I sit in my room with the same clothes on, and I keep thinking I’ll change or wash something, but then I don’t. I used to knit sometimes, and I had a journal, and I’d go walking if it wasn’t too hot, but now it’s like… there’s no push in me.

When my mom asks what’s wrong, I barely even have the energy to answer her. Sometimes I just say “nothing” because explaining feels too much. So maybe I look less emotional, yeah, but I don’t know if that started before the shut-down or if people only noticed once I stopped doing things.
When you were having the concerns about the emails, did you hear voices then?

I don’t know… I don’t think I would call them voices exactly. Like, when I was reading the emails, I’d hear the words in my head the way you do when you read something, but that’s not the same, right?

Sometimes after I read them I’d keep thinking about the wording over and over, and it sort of stayed with me. Like when a teacher writes “please review” and it looks normal, but the way it sits there feels pointed. Sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

So… no, I’m not sure I heard voices then. I was mostly focused on the messages themselves.
For at least one month, were you having the beliefs about the emails during a time when you were not feeling shut down or unable to do things?

Yeah… I think so. It’s hard to separate it neatly, because everything kind of runs together, but the email thing—like the school portal comments and the practicum messages feeling like they were marking me—that’s been pretty fixed for, I guess, about two months now.

And at the start of that, I wasn’t just completely shut down yet. I was still checking things and trying to keep up, even though the wording would get stuck in my head. So yes… at least a month, I think.
Have you heard voices that other people could not hear for at least one month?

For a month… I don’t know. I don’t think so? I mean, sometimes I think I hear my mom say something and then she didn’t, but that could just be the TV or the hallway, because sound carries weird in our house.

It’s not like there’s someone talking to me all day or anything. I get words stuck in my head, especially from emails, and then I keep sort of replaying them, but that feels more like my own head being noisy. Sorry, I’m not answering right. I’m not sure I’ve heard voices other people couldn’t hear for a whole month.
During this shut-down period, have you felt down or depressed most of the day nearly every day?

I don’t know if I’d say depressed most of the day. I was kind of… shut down, like everything felt too much and I didn’t want to deal with things. But “depressed” sounds so specific.

Some days I mostly just stayed in my room, but then I’d also get distracted by stupid stuff, like organizing the same pile of papers or rereading something online and losing time. So I’m not sure. Maybe down sometimes, but nearly every day most of the day… I don’t know.
During the time you were having those beliefs about the emails, did you also feel depressed?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I felt bad, but I don’t know if that’s the same as depressed. Like sometimes I’d just sit there staring at the emails and then I’d end up thinking about completely different things, like whether I should clean my desk or if I forgot to wash a mug downstairs, and then an hour would go by.

So… maybe I felt upset or worn out during it, but I don’t know if I’d call it depressed exactly. It’s hard for me to separate.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has ever been a period of at least two weeks with loss of pleasure in usual activities, to distinguish a depressive episode from primary psychotic or adjustment disorders.
doctor.question: For two weeks or longer, have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

target_item.name: Negative_Symptoms
target_item.manifestation: Mostly I just can't make myself do anything anymore—I sit in my room with the same clothes on, don't knit or journal or go walking like I used to, and when my mom asks what's wrong I barely have the energy to answer.
target_item.reason: The question asks about loss of interest or pleasure in usual activities, which is directly reflected in the negative symptoms profile describing diminished motivation and not doing previously enjoyed activities like knitting, journaling, or walking.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I guess so. I used to knit sometimes, and I had this journal with like different pens—my mom bought me these ones that don’t smear, because I hate when it smears on the side of my hand—and I used to go walking too.

But now mostly I just sit in my room. Same clothes on, not really doing anything. It’s not like I decide, “I don’t like those things anymore,” it’s more like I can’t make myself start. My mom asks what’s wrong and I barely even have the energy to answer her, and then she thinks I’m ignoring her, but I’m not… I just can’t.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient has ever had a full manic episode, which would shift the diagnosis away from depressive and schizophrenia-spectrum options currently under consideration.
doctor.question: Have you ever had a time when you felt so energetic or unusually up that you needed much less sleep than usual?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about manic or hypomanic symptoms, specifically unusually elevated energy and decreased need for sleep, which is not covered by the provided symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
I don’t think so… not like energetic. I mean, sometimes I don’t sleep right, but it’s not because I’m up doing a bunch of things or feeling great. It’s more like I’m just there, awake, and then the room feels too quiet, and I start noticing the little light from the charger, and then I remember I was supposed to wash that hoodie, but then I don’t.

So… no, I don’t really have those times where I’m unusually up and needing less sleep.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic symptoms have persisted for at least one month, to distinguish schizophreniform disorder from major depressive disorder with psychotic features or brief/reactive conditions.
doctor.question: For at least one month, have you believed that the school emails and assignment comments were meant to mark and single you out?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: Since I was in those college classes, I've known the school portal and the clinic practicum people were using little wording changes in emails and assignment comments to mark me as someone they don't want in healthcare, even when my mom says they're just regular messages.
target_item.reason: The question is directly asking about the fixed belief that school emails and assignment comments were meant to mark and single the patient out.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I mean, it was longer than a month. Since I was in those college classes, I kept noticing the school portal messages and the comments on assignments, like little wording changes… not obvious if you’re not looking, but they were there.

And then the clinic practicum people too, like the way they phrased things, it felt like they were marking me out, like saying I wasn’t someone they wanted in healthcare. My mom kept saying they were just normal emails, like “everyone gets those,” but she doesn’t see the pattern because she doesn’t read them the way I do.

It’s hard to explain because if I give one example it sounds small, but it kept happening.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has been at least a two-week period of psychotic symptoms without prominent mood symptoms, to distinguish a schizophrenia-spectrum disorder from major depressive disorder with psychotic features or adjustment disorder.
doctor.question: Was there ever a time when you were having those beliefs about the emails, but you were not also feeling shut down or unable to do things?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: Since I was in those college classes, I've known the school portal and the clinic practicum people were using little wording changes in emails and assignment comments to mark me as someone they don't want in healthcare, even when my mom says they're just regular messages.
target_item.reason: The question is most directly asking about the timing of the fixed beliefs about the school emails and assignment comments, which corresponds to the delusions item.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I think so. It wasn’t only when I was shut down. The email thing was already happening when I was still in the college classes, like before I was just sitting in my room all day.

I’d be looking at the school portal and the assignment comments, and the little wording changes were there. And the clinic practicum people too, the way they wrote things… it felt like they were marking me, like they knew I wasn’t supposed to be in healthcare. My mom kept saying, “That’s just a normal message,” but she doesn’t—she doesn’t look at it the same way.

Sorry, I’m trying to answer. Yes, the messages were still like that even when I wasn’t completely unable to do things.

inference.note: Psychotic symptoms (fixed persecutory/reference delusion about emails) were present for over a month and occurred outside the shut-down/depressive period, which raises a primary schizophrenia-spectrum disorder and makes F20.0 more likely while lowering F43.2. Clear 2+ week anhedonia/avolition supports a depressive episode, but recurrentity remains unclear, so both single and recurrent psychotic/severe depressive possibilities remain; residual schizophrenia (F20.5) is less supported by active delusions.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient has experienced negative symptoms outside of a depressive episode, which would help distinguish schizophrenia from major depressive disorder with psychotic features or schizoaffective disorder.
doctor.question: Before this shut-down period began, did other people say you had become less emotional or less expressive than usual?

target_item.name: Negative_Symptoms
target_item.manifestation: Mostly I just can't make myself do anything anymore—I sit in my room with the same clothes on, don't knit or journal or go walking like I used to, and when my mom asks what's wrong I barely have the energy to answer.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about reduced emotional expression before the shut-down period, which is a negative symptom.

patient.answer:
Before? Um… I don’t know if they said it exactly like that. My mom says I don’t answer her like I used to, but that’s more now, I think.

Mostly I just can’t make myself do anything anymore. I sit in my room with the same clothes on, and I keep thinking I’ll change or wash something, but then I don’t. I used to knit sometimes, and I had a journal, and I’d go walking if it wasn’t too hot, but now it’s like… there’s no push in me.

When my mom asks what’s wrong, I barely even have the energy to answer her. Sometimes I just say “nothing” because explaining feels too much. So maybe I look less emotional, yeah, but I don’t know if that started before the shut-down or if people only noticed once I stopped doing things.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the persecutory belief has been accompanied by hallucinations outside the mood episode, which would help distinguish schizophrenia from schizoaffective disorder and psychotic depression.
doctor.question: When you were having the concerns about the emails, did you hear voices then?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about hearing voices, which refers to hallucinations, but the provided symptom profile does not include hallucinations.

patient.answer:
I don’t know… I don’t think I would call them voices exactly. Like, when I was reading the emails, I’d hear the words in my head the way you do when you read something, but that’s not the same, right?

Sometimes after I read them I’d keep thinking about the wording over and over, and it sort of stayed with me. Like when a teacher writes “please review” and it looks normal, but the way it sits there feels pointed. Sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

So… no, I’m not sure I heard voices then. I was mostly focused on the messages themselves.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic beliefs have persisted for at least one month in the absence of prominent mood symptoms, to distinguish schizophrenia from schizoaffective disorder or major depressive disorder with psychotic features.
doctor.question: For at least one month, were you having the beliefs about the emails during a time when you were not feeling shut down or unable to do things?

target_item.name: Psychotic Symptoms Duration
target_item.manifestation: The beliefs about the school portal and practicum emails marking me have been this fixed for about the past two months.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the fixed beliefs about the emails were present for at least one month, which most directly concerns the duration of the psychotic symptoms.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I think so. It’s hard to separate it neatly, because everything kind of runs together, but the email thing—like the school portal comments and the practicum messages feeling like they were marking me—that’s been pretty fixed for, I guess, about two months now.

And at the start of that, I wasn’t just completely shut down yet. I was still checking things and trying to keep up, even though the wording would get stuck in my head. So yes… at least a month, I think.

inference.note: Evidence now supports a psychotic disorder independent of mood for at least 1 month (fixed persecutory delusion about emails present before and outside the shut-down period), which rules against mood disorders with psychotic features as primary diagnoses (F32.3, F33.3) and makes non-psychotic depressive episodes (F32.2, F33.2) insufficient. Remaining differential is schizophrenia vs schizoaffective depressive type.

doctor.intent: Determine whether hallucinations have been present for at least one month outside of mood symptoms, which would favor schizoaffective disorder over schizophrenia if present with the depressive episode pattern already suggested.
doctor.question: Have you heard voices that other people could not hear for at least one month?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about hearing voices other people could not hear (auditory hallucinations), which is not covered by the provided symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
For a month… I don’t know. I don’t think so? I mean, sometimes I think I hear my mom say something and then she didn’t, but that could just be the TV or the hallway, because sound carries weird in our house.

It’s not like there’s someone talking to me all day or anything. I get words stuck in my head, especially from emails, and then I keep sort of replaying them, but that feels more like my own head being noisy. Sorry, I’m not answering right. I’m not sure I’ve heard voices other people couldn’t hear for a whole month.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has been a sustained major depressive mood episode, which would distinguish schizoaffective disorder, depressive type, from schizophrenia.
doctor.question: During this shut-down period, have you felt down or depressed most of the day nearly every day?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about depressive mood most of the day nearly every day, but the provided symptom profile covers negative symptoms such as low motivation and reduced activity, not depressed mood specifically.

patient.answer:
I don’t know if I’d say depressed most of the day. I was kind of… shut down, like everything felt too much and I didn’t want to deal with things. But “depressed” sounds so specific.

Some days I mostly just stayed in my room, but then I’d also get distracted by stupid stuff, like organizing the same pile of papers or rereading something online and losing time. So I’m not sure. Maybe down sometimes, but nearly every day most of the day… I don’t know.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there was a major depressive episode during the period of psychotic symptoms, to distinguish schizophrenia from schizoaffective disorder, depressive type.
doctor.question: During the time you were having those beliefs about the emails, did you also feel depressed?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about feeling depressed during the period of email-related beliefs, but the symptom profile does not include a depression or mood-symptom item.

patient.answer:
I’m not really sure. I mean, I felt bad, but I don’t know if that’s the same as depressed. Like sometimes I’d just sit there staring at the emails and then I’d end up thinking about completely different things, like whether I should clean my desk or if I forgot to wash a mug downstairs, and then an hour would go by.

So… maybe I felt upset or worn out during it, but I don’t know if I’d call it depressed exactly. It’s hard for me to separate.

inference.note: Ruled out F25.1 because there is at least one month of fixed persecutory delusional beliefs occurring outside any clear depressive episode, and sustained major mood episode criteria are not established. Persistent psychosis with prominent delusions and negative symptoms is most consistent with F20.0.

opening_question.intent: Learn the patient’s main reason for seeking care today
opening_question.question: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a persistent, fixed persecutory delusion that school/practicum communications were coded to mark and single them out, lasting longer than one month and present for at least a month outside any clear mood episode. Hallucinations are not confirmed, but schizophrenia can be diagnosed with persistent delusions plus negative symptoms/functional decline. There is marked avolition, social withdrawal, reduced activity, poor self-care, diminished responsiveness, and loss of interest, with no clear evidence of a sustained major depressive episode or mania accounting for the presentation.
